messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 3287654321 — GPU pool 'eu-west-1-gpu-7' reached 100% capacity, autoscaler failing to provision. queue_length=4123, avg_latency_tokens=280ms, error_rate=5%. Pager routed to #incidents and @jen (oncall).
jen (oncall): ack. I'm online, grabbing console now. Details? any recent deploys?
sara (eng-sre): seeing repeated autoscaler errors: `scaleUp failed: backoff limit reached` in controller logs. also 429s from provider when requesting new instances.
leo (eng-runtime): linked: model-serving pods in that pool are CPU/GPU pinned; some jobs are long-running (>6h) with heavy KV-cache retention. Could be capacity fragmentation.
mike (customer-ops): getting inbound pings from two customers in eu-west with elevated latency for embeddings and chat. No total outage but degraded responses and some timeouts.
jen (oncall): setting incident channel to live. triage owners: @sara for autoscale, @leo for runtime, @nate for infra provider tickets. mike can keep customer comms. tay pls keep product aware.
tay (product): on it — tallying affected customers, escalate to enterprise ops if SLA breach risk.
sara (eng-sre): paste of controller tail:```
2026-06-11T02:14:08Z autoscaler controller scaleUp failed: providerAPI.PersistentError: rate limit exceeded (429)
2026-06-11T02:14:08Z autoscaler controller retrying after backoff (attempt 6)
2026-06-11T02:14:10Z pool-allocator: insufficient contiguous GPUs for pod allocation
```
leo (eng-runtime): also seeing OOM evictions on a couple of pods that pinned >50GB each; fragmentation preventing bin-packing.
jen (oncall): immediate mitigations — 1) divert new non-SLA requests to fallback pool; 2) reduce batch sizes on embeddings to free cache; 3) manually allocate reserve instances if provider allows. who can run the routing change?
nate (infra): I can flip routing for non-dedicated traffic to reserve pool 'eu-west-fallback-1' but need thumbs up — I'll run `rwctl route update --region eu-west --policy best-effort --selector non-sla`
jen (oncall): do it. mike, announce to customers on a best-effort basis and note degraded performance only.
mike (customer-ops): posted status to affected customers: "We're seeing elevated latency for inference in eu-west; traffic routed to fallback pools. No data loss. Working on provisioning additional capacity."
sara (eng-sre): config change: reduced autoscaler aggressive backoff from 5m to 1m for this incident to allow faster retrying. note: provider quotas still showing 0 available.
leo (eng-runtime): lowering default embeddings batch size from 64->32 for eu-west route. Might reduce throughput but helps reduce mem pressure. Pushing hot config now.
jen (oncall): commands used:```
# route change
rwctl route update --region eu-west --policy best-effort --selector non-sla --from-pool eu-west-1-gpu-7 --to-pool eu-west-fallback-1
# manual reserve allocation (if provider accepts)
rwctl capacity allocate --pool eu-west-fallback-1 --count 4 --type g4dn.xlarge
```
nate (infra): provider console shows 4 instances accepted, but provisioning stuck at 60% due to image pull timeout. I've re-triggered image bake and requeued.
sara (eng-sre): meanwhile we've enabled queue throttling for low-priority routes to keep real-time customers stable: `queue.max_inflight=200` for best-effort.
leo (eng-runtime): runtime metrics improving: KV cache eviction rate down 18%, queue length dropped from 4.1k -> 900 after routing change and throttles. latency back to ~120-160ms for priority traffic.
jen (oncall): good. tagging incident INC-2026-0045. assigning owner for mitigation timeline: sara lead, leo runtime fixes, nate provider follow-up. mike will draft customer update.
mike (customer-ops): customers acknowledged. queued a scheduled message for 20m updates.
tay (product): raising severity to SEV2 since some SLA risk for enterprise customers in region. recommending follow-up postmortem.
sara (eng-sre): root cause hypothesis: provider-side 429s + autoscaler backoff + capacity fragmentation from long-running high-memory pods. Need to validate with provider support ticket.
leo (eng-runtime): temporary runtime tweak: enable aggressive KV cache compaction for pods >8h to free memory earlier. rolling now.
jen (oncall): monitoring for 30m. if queue length < 1k and provider continues provision, start scaledown of long-running low-priority pods with 5m drain.
incident-bot: NOTE: page resolved for escalation? ack from oncall recorded.
(30m later)
jen (oncall): update: queue 400, latency stable for priority lanes. provider provisioning completed 4 instances. autoscaler still under observation but not failing. moving to recovery phase.
mike (customer-ops): updated customers: mitigation in place, performance returning, next update in 3h.
sara (eng-sre): creating follow-up tasks: ACTION-1: tighten autoscaler observability + add metric for provider 429s. ACTION-2: implement reserved mini-pool for fast fallback (config + cost calc). ACTION-3: change autoscaler backoff to dynamic policy when queue growth rate > X. ACTION-4: reduce default embeddings batch size only for eu regions when mem pressure high.
leo (eng-runtime): cross-team PR planned to add graceful KV cache compaction and eviction policy per-pod-age. references: `#issue-4923` in repo.
nate (infra): provider ticket 789102 opened referencing our incidents. asking for quota bump and investigation into image pull hotspots.
tay (product): I want a short postmortem summary for execs — include impact window, customers affected, mitigations, and next steps. mike can we get customer list + SLA exposure?
mike (customer-ops): will share list in private thread and copy to postmortem doc.
jen (oncall): closing timeline notes: incident open at 3287654321, mitigations applied by 3287654382, recovery declared at 3287654460. assigning postmortem owner: sara. Finish postmortem draft in 72h.
sara (eng-sre): noted. I'll include timeline, root cause analysis, and the 4 action items.
jen (oncall): thanks team. leaving a short runbook update for future: add quick checklist for routing-to-fallback and reserve allocation examples. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0045 status updated to RECOVERED.
